key_insight: An effective noise threshold marks the boundary between reliable and unreliable QAOA approximation regimes, generally requiring lower noise as circuit depth increases.
engineering_relevance: Depth-dependent thresholds can guide QAOA circuit selection and hardware noise priorities rather than assuming deeper circuits improve optimisation.
method: Simulate noisy QAOA for MaxCut using GPU acceleration.
Fit approximation ratios with a generalised logistic surface.
Use the surface's inflection boundary to define thresholds and three noise-tolerance regions.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covered three graph families with 6–18 vertices, depths up to 10 and three noise channels, with an additional assessment on ibm_marrakesh.
watch_item: Modelled gate errors understated actual hardware noise, so fitted thresholds should not be treated as guarantees of device performance.
paper_title: Effective Noise Thresholds for Reliable Quantum Approximation Optimisation Algorithm under Noisy Environment
